item.title: Former German Intelligence Chief August Hanning arrested on alleged treason and espionage charges

item.content:encoded:
Former German Intelligence Chief August Hanning arrested on alleged treason and espionage charges In an official statement, the Federal Prosecutor’s Office announced that the two German nationals were taken into custody on Tuesday, in Bad Tölz-Wolfratshausen County, Bavaria, and Steinfurt County, North Rhine-Westphalia, pursuant to warrants issued by the Investigating Judge at the Federal Court of Justice. Law enforcement officers simultaneously searched properties in both locations as well as in Berlin. ANI | Updated: 06-10-2026 20:29 IST | Created: 06-10-2026 20:29 IST

Former General Federal Intelligence Service (BND) President August Hanning (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Germany's Federal Criminal Police Office agents have arrested former Federal Intelligence Service (BND) President August Hanning and his former chief of staff, Manfred D, on serious charges including treasonous espionage, spying on state secrets, attempted treason, and espionage, Euro News reported. In an official statement, the Federal Prosecutor’s Office announced that the two German nationals were taken into custody on Tuesday, in Bad Tölz-Wolfratshausen County, Bavaria, and Steinfurt County, North Rhine-Westphalia, pursuant to warrants issued by the Investigating Judge at the Federal Court of Justice. Law enforcement officers simultaneously searched properties in both locations as well as in Berlin. Hanning, who served as President of the BND from December 1998 to November 2005 and later as State Secretary at the Federal Ministry of the Interior between December 2005 and November 2009, is "strongly suspected of treasonous espionage, spying out state secrets, attempted treason, and espionage." Manfred D, who served as Hanning's chief of staff at the BND and parliamentary assistant at the Interior Ministry before resuming duties as chief of staff for several subsequent BND presidents from March 2012 to March 2026, is charged with "aiding and abetting attempted treason and treasonous espionage." According to federal prosecutors, the two suspects agreed in the spring of 2010 that Manfred D would systematically leak confidential intelligence files to Hanning in exchange for payment. Over the years, Manfred D allegedly provided Hanning with approximately 2,000 documents, many containing restricted intelligence intended strictly for internal agency use and executive briefings involving senior officials from federal ministries and German security agencies at the Federal Chancellery. Investigators revealed that Hanning utilised the classified material to enhance his private consultancy services. Prosecutors stated that on one occasion, Hanning "used classified intelligence provided by Manfred D. to draft an analysis for an officer of a foreign intelligence service," though it remains undetermined if the report reached its destination. Furthermore, Hanning was "in close contact with a representative of another foreign intelligence service, to whom he passed on political information, partially based on material provided by Manfred D., for several years." The wide-ranging probe originated after a search of Hanning's property by Hamburg prosecutors in September 2025 during an investigation involving German businesswoman Christina Block and alleged leaks from the Chancellery. Euronews, citing reports by the German newspaper Süddeutsche Zeitung, along with public broadcasters WDR and NDR, previously pointed to evidence uncovered during those proceedings regarding the unauthorised handling of sensitive state documents. The Federal Prosecutor's Office officially took over the investigation in early May 2026, conducting the probe alongside the BND and the Federal Criminal Police Office. Both suspects were brought before the Investigating Judge at the Federal Court of Justice to review the charges and determine pre-trial detention. (ANI)

item.title: China’s alleged expanding espionage network raises global security concerns
item.description: The concerns follow an unprecedented alert issued by Britain’s domestic intelligence agency MI5 on September 30 regarding academic research allegedly linked to China’s Ministry of State Security (MSS) ...
item.content:encoded:
China’s alleged expanding espionage network raises global security concerns The concerns follow an unprecedented alert issued by Britain’s domestic intelligence agency MI5 on September 30 regarding academic research allegedly linked to China’s Ministry of State Security (MSS), according to The Epoch Times. ANI | Updated: 06-10-2026 19:35 IST | Created: 06-10-2026 19:35 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

China’s expanding espionage and technology-gathering activities are raising concerns over national security, critical infrastructure and democratic societies, with analysts warning that stolen data and advanced technologies could be used for surveillance, cyber operations and political interference, The Epoch Times reported. The concerns follow an unprecedented alert issued by Britain’s domestic intelligence agency MI5 on September 30 regarding academic research allegedly linked to China’s Ministry of State Security (MSS), according to The Epoch Times. The Epoch Times reported that more than 100 UK-linked academics had contributed to projects connected with China’s civilian intelligence agency. The newspaper said funding for some of the research was channelled through the China General Technology Research Institute (CGTRI) into areas including artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and other advanced technologies. According to The Epoch Times, MI5 said CGTRI’s primary purpose was to support academic research that could improve the technical capabilities of the MSS for espionage. British authorities have also warned that institutions or individuals continuing to participate in such projects could face legal consequences under the UK’s National Security Act, passed in 2023 to strengthen measures against foreign espionage and hostile state activity. The Epoch Times also reported on a separate case in Germany, where police arrested a married couple in Munich in May over allegations of spying for China by establishing contacts with academics working in aerospace engineering, computer science and artificial intelligence. Lin Tzuli, director of the Center for China and Regional Development at Taiwan’s Tunghai University, told The Epoch Times that China’s alleged espionage, technology theft and cyber activities could create risks extending beyond individual countries. Lin said compromised data could facilitate more sophisticated cross-border surveillance, allowing Chinese intelligence agencies to monitor the communications and movements of targeted individuals. He further warned that intelligence obtained through such activities could provide covert access points into critical infrastructure, potentially creating vulnerabilities that could be exploited during a crisis. According to The Epoch Times, Lin also said Beijing could combine intelligence gathered through data collection with generative AI to make political influence operations more targeted. He suggested that harvested information could be used to identify social divisions before synthetic audio, video and coordinated online messaging are deployed to influence different groups. The developments have intensified debate in Western countries over the security implications of international academic collaboration, research funding and access to emerging technologies. (ANI)

item.title: Egypt, Lebanon, Oman, Greece, Cyprus keen to join IMEC; ministerial meet likely later this year: France
item.description: Egypt, Lebanon, Oman, Greece and Cyprus have expressed interest in joining the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC), French President’s Special Envoy for IMEC Gérard Mestrallet said on ...
item.content:encoded:
Egypt, Lebanon, Oman, Greece, Cyprus keen to join IMEC; ministerial meet likely later this year: France  Egypt, Lebanon, Oman, Greece and Cyprus have expressed interest in joining the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC), French President’s Special Envoy for IMEC Gérard Mestrallet said on Tuesday, adding that an IMEC ministerial meeting is expected to be held later this year to consider expanding the corridor’s membership. ANI | Updated: 06-10-2026 19:27 IST | Created: 06-10-2026 19:27 IST

French President’s Special Envoy for IMEC Gérard Mestrallet (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

By Vishu Adhana Egypt, Lebanon, Oman, Greece and Cyprus have expressed interest in joining the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC), French President’s Special Envoy for IMEC Gérard Mestrallet said on Tuesday, adding that an IMEC ministerial meeting is expected to be held later this year to consider expanding the corridor’s membership. Mestrallet, who is visiting India from October 5-7 to advance the IMEC project and France-India cooperation on connectivity, said any decision to expand the corridor would have to be taken by its eight existing signatory governments. “We have eight signatories and they are heads of state. Potential extension will only be decided by the eight governments. We hope that in the ministerial meeting we could decide to extend the perimeter of IMEC,” Mestrallet said at a press conference in New Delhi. He specifically named Egypt, Lebanon and Oman among countries interested in working with or joining the corridor, while identifying Greece and Cyprus as two European countries that would be particularly keen to become full members. Mestrallet also clarified that Jordan and Israel, although not among the eight original signatories, were mentioned in the initial agreement. “They have not signed because they were not present. It’s Jordan and Israel, although they were mentioned,” he said. The IMEC was announced in September 2023 by India, the United States, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, France, Germany, Italy and the European Union. The ambitious connectivity initiative envisages linking India with Europe through the Arabian Peninsula using a combination of shipping, rail and other connectivity infrastructure. Mestrallet said that since the creation of IMEC, the participating countries have so far held meetings at the steering committee level, but there has not yet been a ministerial-level meeting. “We hope that by the end of this year there will be a ministerial meeting because in the meantime, since the creation of IMEC, there was only a steering committee, not a ministerial committee,” he said. He stressed that only a ministerial meeting involving the existing governments could decide whether the corridor’s geographical and membership perimeter should be expanded. At the same time, Mestrallet said IMEC would have to work with countries and ports outside the original group irrespective of whether they eventually become full members. “In any case, members or not members, we will have to work with them because they want to work positively, and so we have to work with them to find the best possible method — being a full member or associated member or something else,” he said. The remarks come amid renewed efforts by the participating countries to move ahead with the corridor, which seeks to establish a multimodal connectivity route linking India to the Middle East and Europe, including through ports, rail networks and associated clean-energy and digital infrastructure. Mestrallet is also scheduled to participate in discussions on green shipping corridors and IMEC ports during his India visit. On Tuesday, he spoke at the IMEC Ports Club Working Day in New Delhi alongside Christophe Castaner, Chairman of the Supervisory Board of the Port of Marseille Fos. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
Pakistan’s power crisis deepens as electricity shortfall crosses 4,000 MW According to ARY News, sources stated that the worsening shortfall has forced power distribution companies (DISCOs) to increase load-shedding across the country. Consumers in both urban and rural areas are reportedly facing three to four hours of power cuts, with the duration of outages increasing suddenly in several areas. ANI | Updated: 06-10-2026 18:43 IST | Created: 06-10-2026 18:43 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Lahore [Pakistan], October 6 (ANI) Pakistan’s electricity crisis has intensified, with the country’s overall power deficit reportedly surpassing 4,000 megawatts as several generation units remain offline and hydropower production declines, as reported by ARY News. According to ARY News, sources stated that the worsening shortfall has forced power distribution companies (DISCOs) to increase load-shedding across the country. Consumers in both urban and rural areas are reportedly facing three to four hours of power cuts, with the duration of outages increasing suddenly in several areas. The situation is particularly difficult in Lahore, where electricity demand has reportedly climbed to around 4,000 megawatts, against an available supply of approximately 3,000 megawatts. This has created a significant gap between demand and supply, adding to pressure on the already strained power distribution system. The latest deterioration has also raised questions over repeated government claims that Pakistan’s electricity shortages had been brought under control. The sources said the promised improvement has failed to materialise as the supply deficit continues to widen. Lahore is also reportedly experiencing a shortage of diesel following disruptions in gas availability, further complicating the city’s energy situation, sources said. Meanwhile, the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (NEPRA) has taken action against K-Electric (KE) over its practice of carrying out load-shedding on feeders based on aggregate technical and commercial (ATC) losses. NEPRA has declared such load-shedding illegal and directed K-Electric to immediately stop unannounced power outages carried out on the basis of feeder losses. The regulator maintained that consumers who regularly pay their electricity bills should not have their supply suspended simply because they are connected to feeders with high losses, as cited by ARY News. NEPRA stressed that paying consumers should not be penalised for electricity theft or other failures by other users. The authority instructed K-Electric to take targeted action against individual consumers involved in electricity theft rather than cutting power to entire feeders, as reported by ARY News. (ANI)
